1	Benchmark contamination is widely assumed to inflate language model scores, yet the actual effect has never been systematically measured across model families. We perform controlled SFT injection at five dosage levels into five models spanning four independent families (7B--14.7B parameters) and discover that contamination produces not one effect but five distinct dose-response patterns: Immune ($\pm$0.5pp), U-type collapse ($-$10pp), V-type recovery ($-$3pp then partial rebound), Benefit ($+$3.8pp monotonic), and Benefit-saturation ($+$3.2pp then plateau). A baseline ability threshold at 64.7\% MMLU (bootstrap 95\% CI: 64.0--65.4\%) separates models that benefit from contamination from those that are harmed or immune. Counter-intuitively, the 14B Qwen model is 3$\times$ more fragile than 7B. Profiles are robust on MMLU (4/5 families $\geq$99.6\% bootstrap stability); ARC-Challenge shows directional agreement for 3/5 families but lower stability due to its smaller item pool (1{,}172 vs.\ 14{,}042 items). We further characterize contamination detection signal failure: Min-K\%++ exhibits directional reversal at small scales (Cohen's $d = -1.55$ to $-1.98$), actively misleading practitioners. Simulation studies establish that IRT-based contamination diagnosis requires ensemble sizes ($J \geq 50$) above current practice. Simulation studies establish that IRT-based contamination diagnosis requires ensemble sizes ($J \geq 50$) above current practice. toolUseResult.originalFile: Benchmark contamination is widely assumed to inflate language model scores, yet the actual effect has never been systematically measured across model families. We perform controlled SFT injection at five dosage levels into five models spanning four independent families (7B--14.7B parameters) and discover that contamination produces not one effect but five distinct dose-response patterns: Immune ($\pm$0.5pp), U-type collapse ($-$10pp), V-type recovery ($-$3pp then partial rebound), Benefit ($+$3.8pp monotonic), and Benefit-saturation ($+$3.2pp then plateau). A baseline ability threshold at 64.7\% MMLU (bootstrap 95\% CI: 64.0--65.4\%) separates models that benefit from contamination from those that are harmed or immune. Counter-intuitively, the 14B Qwen model is 3$\times$ more fragile than 7B. Profiles are robust on MMLU (4/5 families $\geq$99.6\% bootstrap stability); ARC-Challenge shows directional agreement for 3/5 families but lower stability due to its smaller item pool (1{,}172 vs.\ 14{,}042 items). We further characterize contamination detection signal failure: Min-K\%++ exhibits directional reversal at small scales (Cohen's $d = -1.55$ to $-1.98$), actively misleading practitioners. Simulation studies establish that IRT-based contamination diagnosis requires ensemble sizes ($J \geq 50$) above current practice. Our findings demonstrate that ``contamination equals inflation'' is a gross oversimplification; model-specific dose-response profiling is necessary for reliable benchmark interpretation.
